how_to_mine: Follow this plan exactly. Each lens agent reads only its pages (all are in the corpus; read them with `show <source_id> --around TEXT` or `--lines A:B`, tables with `tables <source_id>`), answers its demand items, and records each item as filled (fact ids), contradicted (what the page says instead) or not-found (where you looked).

Write facts in files of 10 to 25 facts: _build/work/34-streaming/facts-<lens>-NN.json (lens file names: numbers, behavior, faq), then `facts add --file <that file> --by mine-34-<lens>`. Table rows and value lines: prefer `facts adopt` (--table/--row, --sentence, --heading). Every quote is copied verbatim from the page snapshot (.txt), never from full.md (full.md hits are pointers) and never from memory.

Each quote must carry every clause, scope, condition and exception of the claim on its own. When the condition stands in the next sentence (for example 'With On-demand Standard and Provisioned streams, you can register up to 20 consumers per stream' next to the 50-consumer sentence, or 'Streaming tables and Amazon S3 delivery require on-demand capacity mode.'), include that sentence in the quote; otherwise narrow the claim. Entail votes run on Opus and mark a clause found only in the surrounding text as partial.

Fact service keys: `kinesis-data-streams` for Kinesis Data Streams facts (ids start with `kinesis-data-streams-`; no short forms such as `kds-`), `data-firehose` for Firehose facts (ids start with `data-firehose-`), `msk` for MSK facts (ids start with `msk-`). Managed Service for Apache Flink is not an in-scope service (registry note): its 'formerly Kinesis Data Analytics' fact, the Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL shutdown fact and the decision-guide streaming facts go under `kinesis-data-streams`. Neighbour facts: SQS `sqs` (chapter 31), Lambda `lambda` (chapter 18), Kinesis Video Streams `kinesis-video-streams` (chapter 36). Add a neighbour fact only after `facts list --service <key>` shows no verified fact that already answers it; reuse the existing id in the demand record when one exists (n-sqs.txt and n-lambda.txt list them).

Two Kinesis facts already exist at mech-pass from another chapter: `kinesis-data-streams-multiple-independent-consumer-applications` and `kinesis-data-streams-decision-streaming-category`. Reuse them; never add a second fact with the same claim.

Every hard fact (number, limit, default, price, date, can/cannot, only/always/never) carries `question` (the demand question it answers) and at least two displays for kinds behavior, capability, restriction and default (brief gate B12). A display of a number-free fact is a verbatim phrase of at most 8 words from its quote (RULINGS 2026-10-11).

Names: write claims with the current names (Amazon Data Firehose, Firehose stream, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink). Where a quote says 'delivery stream' or 'Kinesis Data Firehose', keep the quote as is; the writer handles 'formerly'.

Scope matters here: many Kinesis statements hold only for provisioned mode, only for on-demand mode, only for On-demand Advantage, or only in three Regions (US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland)). Many Firehose numbers hold only for Direct PUT, only for S3, or only in some Regions. Many MSK statements hold only for Standard brokers, only for Express brokers or only for MSK Serverless. Put that scope in the claim and make sure the quote states it.

Changes: a fact touched by a change item sets `changed` (date, old value only if a saved page states it verbatim) and `change_items`. A feature GA after 2026-07-15 gets the note `not examinable yet`: KDS data delivery to S3 and streaming tables (2026-08-29), KDS service-managed partition keys (2026-09-23), KDS warm-throughput scale-down (2026-07-24), KDS dry run (2026-09-01), MSK ZooKeeper-to-KRaft in-place migration (2026-08-10), MSK Express data delivery to S3 and Iceberg (2026-07-30), MSK custom domain names (2026-08-17). Current truth comes from the guide, quotas and pricing pages; What's New pages and history rows give dates and deltas only.
Case-study facts have kind `case-study` and a quote of at most 25 words.

numbers+changes.job: Every number, limit, default and price for Kinesis Data Streams, Data Firehose and MSK: the KDS quota page and capacity-mode page first (shard throughput, record size, retention, on-demand defaults and maxima, shard quotas, enhanced fan-out consumers, mode switching, UpdateShardCount and data-plane API limits), then the Firehose buffering hints and quota page, then the MSK quota tables (Standard, Express, Serverless), then the three pricing pages (dimensions and units; prefer dimension facts over Regional per-hour prices) and the SLA pages. Then one change fact per change item listed in demand d009, d010, d016 and d020 with the date from the history row or the change-feed row (What's New pages fetched for 2025 and 2026 only) and a pointer to the current-truth fact. Kinds: limit, quota, default, price, change.
watch: The stream and shard quota table at the top of service-sizes-and-limits is raw HTML (<table>, <td>), not a Markdown table: `tables` lists only the two API-limit tables below it. Quote whole sentences from inside one <td> cell (for example 'Each shard can support up to 1 MB/sec or 1,000 records/sec write throughput or up to 2 MB/sec or 2,000 records/sec read throughput.'), and say in the claim which column (On-demand mode or Provisioned mode) the cell sits in; when the cell has colspan=2 it applies to both modes.

On-demand maxima differ by Region: 10 GB/s write and 20 GB/s read only in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon) and Europe (Ireland); 200 MB/s and 400 MB/s elsewhere. The default shard quota is 20,000 only in those three Regions and '1,000 or 6,000' elsewhere. Keep the Region scope in the claim and the quote.

Enhanced fan-out: 50 registered consumers only with On-demand Advantage and only in the Regions the page lists; 20 for On-demand Standard and Provisioned. The 'Important' paragraph of enhanced-consumers holds both sentences: quote both.

Record size (d002): the quota page says 'up to 10 MiB' and 'intermittent large records (1-10MiB in size) using burst capacity'. Read large-records for the default maximum (1 MiB) and how the limit is raised; the 1 MB/s per-shard write limit still applies. Do not write '10 MiB by default'.

Retention (d003): 'default of 24 hours' and 'up to 8760 hours (365 days)' are on key-concepts and kinesis-extended-retention; the 7-day boundary between extended and long-term retention is a pricing term on the pricing page and the FAQ.

What's New pages from 2020 to 2024 are disallowed by robots.txt (brief fetch_failures): for the on-demand 10 GB/s (2024-11-20), MSK Express GA (2024-11-07) and Firehose zero buffering (2023-12-26) dates use the change-feed row (changes for <service>) or the doc-history row, never memory.

Firehose limits page has no Markdown tables (bullet list text): use `facts adopt --sentence` or quote whole bullet lines with the heading. Direct PUT throughput differs by Region (higher in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland)); keep the Region list. The record size limit is 'before base64-encoding'.
MSK quota tables carry a 'Notes' column with conditions (per account vs per cluster, adjustable or not, Standard vs Express): adopt the row with its header so the condition stays in the quote.

Pricing numbers vary by Region and change often: prefer dimension facts (what is charged and its unit, the 25 KB PUT payload unit, the 5 KB rounding for Firehose Direct PUT, the 60% lower On-demand Advantage data prices) over per-hour dollar values; a price fact names its Region as the page shows it.

Not examinable yet (GA after 2026-07-15): KDS S3 delivery and streaming tables, service-managed partition keys, warm-throughput scale-down, dry run, MSK ZooKeeper-to-KRaft in-place migration, MSK Express S3 and Iceberg delivery. Add the fact with that note; the writer puts it in 'Changed recently' only.

behavior+decisions.job: Every behaviour, capability, restriction and decision rule the exam uses: Kinesis Data Streams concepts (partition key, shard, ordering, sequence number), several consumers and replay, producers and consumers (KPL, Agent, KCL, Lambda, Flink, Firehose, enhanced fan-out), hot shards and throttling, duplicates, encryption, VPC endpoints, IAM and resource policies, resilience, monitoring, latency; Firehose purpose, destinations, sources, transformation, format conversion, dynamic partitioning, delivery and failure handling, security, cross-account delivery, logs-to-S3 paths; MSK purpose, deployment options, security and connectivity, resilience, integrations; the comparisons SQS vs KDS, KDS vs Firehose, KDS vs MSK, and the neighbours Video Streams and Managed Service for Apache Flink; whitepaper patterns and the decision guide; Lambda event source settings (reuse lambda facts); the Callvale decision facts (d052 lists ids); one or two case studies. Kinds: behavior, capability, restriction, default, decision, case-study.
tools: show docs/streams/latest/dev/how-do-i-size-a-stream --around "Handle read and write throughput exceptions" --chars 3000
watch: Ordering (d021): ordering holds per shard, for records with the same partition key; there is no ordering across shards. The service-managed record distribution pages (2026-09-23, not examinable yet) say 'No ordering guarantees' for that strategy only; never generalise it to the stream.

Replay and several consumers (d022): the claim 'records are not removed when read' needs a sentence that says so; if no page states it, narrow the claim to 'a consumer can re-read records within the retention period' with the iterator types as evidence.

Encryption (d027): be precise about which key options exist (AWS managed key aws/kinesis, customer managed key) and whether SSE is the default for new streams; do not write 'encrypted by default' unless a page says it verbatim with its scope.

Firehose 'near real-time' (d032, d033): use the FAQ answer on how often Firehose delivers to S3 and the buffering section; with zero buffering the delivery is within seconds. Keep the buffering condition in the claim.

Firehose one-destination questions (d038, d055): the FAQ answers for multiple S3 buckets, Redshift tables and OpenSearch domains are separate items; quote each answer whole, they may contain 'Currently' or exceptions (Iceberg and Snowflake can route to several tables).

MSK public access (d042): public access is off by default and has preconditions (Kafka version, broker type, authentication, encryption); a claim 'MSK cannot be reached from the internet' is wrong as a universal. Quote the conditions list or narrow the claim.
MSK Serverless (d041, d042): authentication is IAM only per the FAQ; confirm on serverless or the FAQ before writing a restriction fact.

SQS comparison (d045): reuse the chapter-31 SQS facts listed in the demand note; add only KDS-side facts and the KDS FAQ comparison answers (FAQ lens may already hold them: check `facts list --service kinesis-data-streams` before adding).
Lambda (d051): reuse the chapter-18 lambda facts listed in the demand note; add only missing items (for example Lambda with MSK).
Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL was fully shut down 2026-01-27 (full_shutdown_services): a fact with that date, so the writer can remove it from answers.
Callvale story values (1,500 events a second, 1 KB, 3 seconds, 6 hours, 3,000 calls) are story data, never facts; d052 lists the AWS facts each reason cites. The story never teaches a fact.

Case studies: VMware, LaunchDarkly, TrueCar, Docebo, AGCO, FactSet, Fox, ShopFully and Behavox redirect to the listing page (brief fetch_failures); use only Taggle Systems, ICCW, Cisco, Deputy 2024, Arity, MarketReader, StreamAMG, Utopus Insights, Pionex. Quotes at most 25 words.

faq.job: Quick-fire FAQ facts for the FAQ section (verbatim FAQ answers, one or two sentences each): the questions listed in d054 (Kinesis Data Streams), d055 (Data Firehose), d056 (MSK) and d057 (security across the three). Each fact quotes the answer sentence(s) whole; the claim keeps the answer's conditions. Kinds: behavior, capability, restriction, decision, limit.
watch: The FAQ lists (work files faq-kds.txt, faq-firehose.txt, faq-msk.txt) give the question numbers used in the demand items; the last item of each list is an empty 'NA' entry, skip it.

FAQ answers can be older than the guide (for example enhanced fan-out consumer counts or on-demand maxima): when a FAQ number disagrees with the quota page, add the quota-page value in the numbers lens, record the conflict in the demand note and do not add the FAQ number as a competing fact.

Before adding a FAQ fact for a number already covered by the numbers lens, check `facts list --service <key>`; the FAQ lens adds the quick-fire sentence only when it states something new or states it in a form the FAQ section quotes.

rules: Quote from page snapshots only; full.md hits are pointers.
A demand item becomes filled, contradicted (with what the page says) or not-found.
Current truth comes from the guide, quotas and pricing pages; What's New pages and history rows give dates and deltas only.
Files of 10 to 25 facts; every quote verbatim and complete for its claim; `--by mine-34-<lens>`.
